title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest subsequence common to strings `text1` and `text2`.
hints: If the last characters match, they belong to some optimal subsequence. Take them and add one.
If they differ, discard one of them. The answer is the better of the two choices.
A rolling row stores only the previous string index.

approaches.name: 2D DP
approaches.explanation: dp[i][j] is the LCS of the prefixes of those lengths.

editorial: dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 when the characters match, otherwise the max of dropping a character from either string. The empty prefix has LCS 0. The bottom-right cell is the answer. Reconstructing the string walks backward through the same decisions.
